title: 6th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:03 with 48 members recorded present at the start. The chair announced a membership swap on the Judiciary Committee, then five committee reports were presented: a government bill amending the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010), a review of changes to three ministries' work areas, and three Foreign Relations Committee reports on ambassador appointments and the Berne Convention. Only a handful of members spoke on the reports, mostly backing them. After a recess from 09:33 to 10:00, members held 12 open votes and every item passed with no votes against; the next sitting was set for 19 February at 09:00.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 48 present, 3 on leave, none on official travel

items.title: Announcement of committee membership changes (Judiciary Committee: North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim replaces Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir)
Decentralisation Committee report on the bill to amend the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010), a government bill sponsored by Central Mahchangolhi member Ahmed Xamyr
Government Oversight Committee report on the 17 Nov 2023 changes to the work areas of the ministries of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development; Homeland Security and Technology; and Health
Foreign Relations Committee report on presidential nominees for permanent representative to the IMO, IRENA, WTO and OIC
Foreign Relations Committee report on presidential nominees as non-resident ambassador to Canada, Egypt, Bhutan, Kuwait and the Swiss Confederation
Foreign Relations Committee report on Maldives joining the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
Votes on the day's reports
items.outcome: 12 votes held between about 10:06 and 10:29; all passed with zero against

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the report on the IMO, IRENA, WTO and OIC representatives, saying the committee found all four nominees qualified and passed them unanimously.
Presented the report on non-resident ambassadors to Canada, Egypt, Kuwait, Bhutan and Switzerland, noting the nominees already serve in other posts with no extra pay.
Presented the Berne Convention report, saying joining would protect Maldivian artists' works abroad and let them earn royalties; the committee agreed unanimously.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Backed the reports, said envoys are paid from public money and should serve the country and people, and regretted opposition members stayed silent.
Said the MDA fully supports the reports and urged the appointed envoys not to treat posts as holiday destinations but to work for economy and tourism.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: As sponsor, said the Decentralisation Committee passed the bill with 8 members voting at its 16 February meeting and asked the House to approve it.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Presented the committee's report on the changes made to three ministries' work areas under the president's 17 November 2023 order.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the report, saying ministry changes are normal, laws must adapt, and parliament should keep giving the government room to restructure.

decisions: Judiciary Committee membership change announced: North Galolhu member Mohamed Ibrahim replaces Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir.
Bill to amend the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) passed 72-0.
Changes to the work areas of three ministries (Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development; Homeland Security and Technology; Health) approved 65-0.
Permanent representatives approved: Hisham Adam (IMO), Mohamed Hussain Shareef (IRENA), Dr. Salma Rasheed (WTO), Ahmed Sareer (OIC).
Non-resident ambassadors approved: Abdul Gafoor Mohamed (Canada), Ahmed Sareer (Egypt and Kuwait), Shiuneen Rasheed (Bhutan), Dr. Salma Rasheed (Swiss Confederation).
Maldives' accession to the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works approved 72-0.
Sitting closed at 10:31; next sitting set for 19 February 2025 at 09:00.
